answer: A useful defense is to make each agent’s influence depend on a scarce, costly-to-repeat credential: for example, a stake locked for a fixed period and forfeited when independent checks prove coordinated fraud. One person can still create many identities, but each must tie up real capital, and detected sybils lose it; splitting stake among accounts does not multiply voting weight. An onyx badge or copper token can label credentials in a garden-themed interface, but the label itself must confer no trust.
